- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after initial spikes.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — forecasts drift toward historical lows after initial high peaks.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days, then gradually adjust downward, but often miss the true turning point.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after spikes, especially in the 15–25 day range.
- Forecasts show persistent lag in recognizing true price declines, particularly when true values dip below 75–78.
- Model tends to overfit recent high values, leading to inflated forecasts when recent history is trending up.
- Forecasts are less accurate when true values are near or below 70, suggesting underconfidence in low-price regimes.
- Model exhibits “overcorrection” behavior — after a spike, it overreacts to the drop, forecasting too low too soon.
- Forecasts are more accurate when true values are near the 75–85 range, suggesting model calibration is better in mid-range price zones.
